reviewed_clauses.source_clause: A zero pairwise bound makes the actual gap constant; a positive gap stays positive everywhere with no finite restriction.

reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The gap equality is derived directly for every two inputs. The positive-gap preservation conclusion is additionally proved by GeneralMargin.actual_zero_gap_gain_preserves_class_pair_everywhere, and covers arbitrary distance without division by zero.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: An actual L-Lipschitz logit map with positive margin keeps its unique predicted class under every perturbation of norm less than margin/(sqrt2 L).
hypotheses: Positive real L; all-input genuine Euclidean logit norm bound; nonempty finite competitors; actual distance less than the stated true maximum-margin quotient.
Euclidean input distance instantiates the proof metric with distance(x,x+delta)=norm(delta); the positive margin is the source condition for a nonempty positive-radius ball.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The actual maximum competitor logit defines the source margin. A genuine Euclidean basis-difference sqrt2 norm bound yields each real gap inequality; all competitor logits are strictly below the winner at the perturbed point, giving unique argmax and deterministic prediction preservation.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: Any positive bounds on the true class gaps give the minimum of the actual gap/bound ratios as a prediction-preserving radius.
hypotheses: All actual competitor bounds are positive, satisfy their true gap-increment inequalities, and the perturbation distance is less than the true finite minimum.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The radius is actual Finset.min' of all source competitors, not an assumed optimal statistic. Each minimum comparison yields its actual gap ratio bound; all competitor inequalities establish unique prediction.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The uniform sqrt2 L gap bound is valid and its actual one-vs-rest minimum equals the global margin divided by sqrt2 L.
hypotheses: A positive uniform gain and true nonempty competitor set; instantiate gain=sqrt2 L with L>0.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: Actual finite maximum/minimum identities are proved, and GeneralMargin derives the sqrt2 L gap bound from the true whole-logit Euclidean bound.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: An affine last layer with actual rows w_i on an Lsub-Lipschitz feature map has true gap bound Lsub*norm(w_y-w_j).
hypotheses: A finite real weight matrix and bias, actual feature map with its all-input Euclidean norm bound; the resulting gain is used in a quotient only when positive or replaced by a positive upper bound.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The actual logits are matrix-vector feature plus bias and the pair gain is the true Euclidean norm of the actual row difference. Bias cancellation and the true inner-product norm inequality prove the universal gap bound. Zero products use the separately established constant-gap case.

reviewed_clauses.source_clause: The radius certificate is a deterministic guarantee that the same chosen class strictly dominates every competitor.
hypotheses: The source positive initial margin, finite at-least-two classes, and the displayed strict radius test.
reviewed_clauses.per_clause_reason: The conclusions are literal all-competitor strict inequalities, which imply the same unique argmax. No empirical accuracy, adversarial existence or probabilistic claim is inferred.

material_units.source_text:
Theorem — Margin certificate (Tsuzuku, Sato & Sugiyama 2018, Props. 1–2)
      
        Assume $N\ge2$. The displayed quotients use positive certificate bounds $L$ and $L_{yj}$; a positive upper bound can always be chosen. If a pairwise bound is zero, the corresponding gap is constant and, when positive at $x$, imposes no finite radius restriction. If the logit map is $L$-Lipschitz in $\ell_2$ and $M_f(x)=f_y(x)-\max_{j\ne y}f_j(x)\gt0$, the prediction cannot change for $\|\delta\|_2\lt M_f(x)/(\sqrt2L)$ (Prop. 1). More generally, if $L_{yj}$ bounds the Lipschitz constant of $f_y-f_j$, the radius is $\min_{j\ne y}\big(f_y(x)-f_j(x)\big)/L_{yj}$; $L_{yj}=\sqrt2L$ is always valid and recovers the first rule, and a last linear layer with rows $w_i$ on top of an $L_{\rm sub}$-Lipschitz feature map gives $L_{yj}=L_{\rm sub}\|w_y-w_j\|$ (Prop. 2).
material_units.per_unit_reason: Every mathematical clause is covered by the precise generic proofs above: true finite margin/radius objects, positive ordinary quotients, constructive positive bound replacement, constant zero-gap exception, actual all-class unique prediction and actual arbitrary-Lsub affine row-norm bound. The named paper attribution was separately verified in its primary text.

primary_source_attribution.exact_scope: The 2018 primary paper section4.1 propositions1 and2 gives the global sqrt2-margin bound and the final-linear-row difference times feature Lipschitz bound. Its strict interior radius supplies the unique-label guarantee used here. The general arbitrary pairwise-bound formulation is a directly proved extension; the correction explicitly supplies finite-competitor and ordinary-quotient edge conditions.

limits: Only exact units744/746/748 are approved. Other classification normalization, literature conventions, empirical accuracy and table claims are not approved by association.

The nonnegative wrappers whose zero antecedent relies on Lean div_zero vacuity are not used to define an ordinary zero-denominator printed quotient. Constant gaps are handled by actual gap equality and unrestricted positive-gap preservation.
A certificate is a sufficient lower bound on robust radius. Neither maximal robust radius nor adversarial existence outside the certificate is asserted.
